On Mon, Jan 23, 2023 at 10:18 AM Garth Willis <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Michael,
I am finally able to circle back to you on this now that we have a version of the Atrocity Prevention /
Tech company engagement framework that while not final, is ready to be shared.
After many conversations with State and the NSC we were able to pare down the NSC vision to have a
much longer list of countries for the pilot phase to 2-4 countries. In discussions with State it was
mutually agreed that two countries that would work well for the pilot phase are Burma and Bangladesh.
This of course is contingent on Regional Bureau/Mission concurrence.
Would you be able to share this with your team? We would be open for a further discussion with any
questions you may have. Also as an FYI NSC is hoping that we can have a workshop with tech
companies in the coming weeks/months where we will discuss the framework broadly, this workshop
will be led by State with support from USAID.
Short term asks would be to get concurrence that Burma and Bangladesh are appropriate for inclusion,
that there is Bureau/Mission buy-in, and a POC for engagement moving forward. As you mentioned
earlier, this can be seen as a good opportunity to get the attention of Tech companies that are active in
the two countries, and to use the inter-agency to bring our perspectives to their approach to monitoring
and responding to events on the ground.
Garth

Hi everyone,
I had a talk with Garth who works with Vera, the Agency MDM lead and is coordinating
the response to this NSC request.
1. We both think it is a good opportunity to engage tech companies in addressing
MDM ahead of elections/critical events.
1. The term 'atrocity prevention' can sound shocking but the framework is similar to
other conflict/violence prevention frameworks including USAID's election security
and election assessment frameworks. Similar to the term anti-corruption, care has
to be used when discussing the issue and using the term with local partners.
1. Garth and his State department counterpart will put forward five countries including
Bangladesh and Burma for consideration to NSC with the caveat that additional
consultation/approval is needed with missions/embassies and regional bureaus.
Theywill also recommend that NSC chooses one country to focus on as a test
case/proof of concept while watching the other four for possible engangement.
Other countries are Zimbabwe, El Salvador, and the Democratic Republic of
Congo.
1.If missions agree, I think we should advocate for an Asia country to get selected,
perhaps Burma given the recent request from AA Schiffer regarding Burma
elections.

In brief, we are looking to engage with Tech companies to prevent and
mitigate mass atrocities where 1) there are upcoming Key Events that could
create a risk of violence or mass atrocities, and 2) where tech platform
engagement could have a mitigating impact on those risks.
We (USAID and State) have been tasked by the WWhite House to separately
prepare a list of up to five counties where we believe the USG can engage
with tech companies to mitigate risks of mass atrocities. We have been
tasked to send this list to the White House by COB on Tuesday 12/13.
Both State and USAID pushed back that this is unreasonable, but the deadline
was set for us. After both State and USAID send their respective lists there will
be another Sub-IPC to crosswalk the two lists to create a final list of countries
for inclusion.
As a group, the USAID representatives on the Sub-IPC came up with a short
list of eight countries that we still need to narrow down to five. At this point we
want to make sure all the Regional Bureaus have eyes on this and can
provide their input, and ideally concurrence, prior to the Tuesday deadline.
The eight countries (in no particular order) are:
1. Burma
2. Bangladesh
3. Pakistan
4. Zimbabwe
5. Democratic Republic of Congo
6. Ethiopia
7. Mali
8. El Salvador

Garth
